newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower amid softer cash.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas called lower amid softer cash.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were expected to open lower Monday amid early talk of softer cash prices, industry sources said.
June over-the-counter trade ranged from $2.08 to $2.10 at 0935 EDT after settling Friday at $2.126 per million British thermal units.
"We're looking next at $2.07 or $2.075. If we can get below that, we might get some more momentum," a market source said, noting a retest of $2 may become possible.
Early cash prices at Henry Hub were talked several cents lower around $2.10 per mmBtu.

Putting some downward pressure on prices were forecasts for near- to above-normal temperatures throughout most of the Northeast and upper Midwest Tuesday and Wednesday before slipping slightly below normal Thursday. In the southern plains and most of the Southwest, temperatures are expected to run a few degrees above normal all week.
After $2.07, technical traders pegged support in June at $2.03 and then along the short-term up trendline around $2.00. Resistance was seen at $2.24 and then at $2.33.

In Friday's cash market, Henry Hub prices firmed more than five cents to $2.15-2.20. May gas at the Gulf was up a similar amount to $2.10-15. April Midcon held relatively steady in the mid-$1.90s, with May on the same pipes up slightly to the mid-to-high $1.90s. April gas in New York gained more than five cents to the mid-$2.40s, while May city gate was up a couple of cents to the mid-$2.40s.
Some air-conditioning demand may emerge by the middle of this week in parts of Texas as temperatures are expected to climb into the high-80s, one trader noted.
This may result in an active aftermarket as nominated May gas begins to flow on Thursday.
